meta.note: Live-wins dedup against existing corpus; geography- and institution-as-a-node scaffolding stripped; see notes/mint-2026-08-20.md

reports.title: Population estimates
reports.description: Population estimates. Population is approximately 43 million; the age structure is very young and conflict-related displacement is large-scale.
reports._url_evidence: UNFPA World Population Dashboard country page for Yemen; page states 'Total Population (2025): 41,800,000' sourced from the UN Population Division (the CSO itself publishes no current population series).
reports._cadence_evidence: UNFPA World Population Dashboard page states the numbers 'come from UNFPA and fellow UN agencies, and are updated annually'; current vintage shown is 2025.

reports.title: National Accounts of Yemen (GDP)
reports.description: National accounts and GDP estimates. The economy has contracted sharply under prolonged conflict; oil production is a fraction of pre-war levels and non-oil activity is severely disrupted.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node under severe conflict constraints.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank document record titled 'Yemen Economic Monitor: Persistent Fragility amid Rising Risks', described as an update on key economic developments over the past six months - the de facto national accounts/GDP estimate series for Yemen.
reports._cadence_evidence: World Bank document is 'Yemen Economic Monitor: Persistent Fragility amid Rising Risks'; the series description says it 'provides an update on key economic developments and policies over the past six months' - a twice-yearly monitor.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.description: CPI and inflation rates. Inflation has been elevated and highly volatile under exchange-rate collapse, supply disruptions and dual-currency conditions.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node under elevated-inflation and dual-rate conditions.
reports._url_evidence: Central Bank of Yemen (Aden) 'Monetary and Financial Developments' monthly report series; the May 2026 issue on this page reports the general consumer price index rising from 98.19 (April 2026) to 100.05 (May 2026).
reports._cadence_evidence: cby-ye.com/pages/28 hosts 'التطورات النقدية والمالية' (Monetary and Financial Developments), one PDF per calendar month running from December 2021 through May 2026.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.description: BOP and external-sector statistics. Oil exports have collapsed; remittances, humanitarian inflows and limited formal trade dominate; reserves are critically low.
reports._notes: External-accounts node under severe constraint and large informal/humanitarian flows.
reports._url_evidence: Central Bank of Yemen annual report series page (2020-2025 editions); the 2024 report linked here contains Chapter Four 'ميزان المدفوعات' (Balance of Payments) with an overall balance deficit of ~USD 774 million and current account -26.6% of GDP.
reports._cadence_evidence: cby-ye.com/pages/31 is the Central Bank's 'التقارير السنوية' (Annual Reports) page, listing one report per year (2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025).

reports.title: Oil production and export statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Oil and IMF-aligned sources
reports.description: Statistics on crude oil production and exports. Production has collapsed from pre-war peaks near 400+ thousand barrels per day to the low tens of thousands (or lower) in recent years; export interruption has been a central fiscal and external shock.
reports._notes: Core (collapsed) extractive node. Highest pre-war centrality; now a defining absence.
reports._url_evidence: IEA Yemen oil country statistics page (breadcrumb Yemen/Middle East, oil supply/production/trade section); figures are rendered client-side so no numbers appear in the fetched text. Yemen's own Ministry of Oil domains (mom.gov.ye, moom.gov.ye) are unreachable via WebFetch.
reports._cadence_evidence: IEA Yemen oil country page carries only explanatory narrative about oil supply and refining; no last-updated date, data vintage, source dataset or update-frequency note appears anywhere on it.

reports.title: Humanitarian needs and food insecurity statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from OCHA / joint monitoring and IPC-aligned sources
reports.description: Statistics on food insecurity and humanitarian needs. Inadequate food consumption affects a majority of the population in recent monitoring; severe deprivation and reliance on crisis coping strategies are widespread across both control areas.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality social and humanitarian node under current conditions.
reports._url_evidence: OCHA's Yemen country page, citing the 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan reprioritised to 8.8 million people and the Yemen Humanitarian Update covering food security and nutrition; IPC's Yemen analysis page (ipcinfo.org, ?iso3=YEM) resolves but currently returns 'No records found'.
reports._cadence_evidence: OCHA Yemen page features the 'Yemen Humanitarian Update - December 2025' situation report; OCHA's own publication listing shows month-labelled editions in a numbered series (Issue 1 Jan-Feb 2024, Issue 2 March 2024, ... September 2025, December 2025, April 2026), i.e. a monthly update.

reports.title: Dual exchange-rate and rial statistics
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Yemen / market monitoring
reports.description: Statistics and framing of the dual exchange-rate regime. Government-controlled and Ansar Allah-controlled areas maintain sharply divergent rial rates; the divergence is a structural feature of the fragmented monetary system and a key driver of inflation differentials.
reports._notes: Critical price and institutional-fragmentation node. Dual rates are a defining structural feature.
reports._url_evidence: CBY (Aden) monthly report series; the May 2026 issue gives the average rial rate at 1,562.49 YER/USD with a 2017-2026 history table. Caveat: as written the item spans a divided institution - this covers only the IRG/Aden rate, and no single official publisher issues both the Aden and Sana'a rates.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same CBY page as the CPI item (pages/28): the exchange-rate and rial figures are carried inside the monthly Monetary and Financial Developments report, monthly editions Dec 2021 - May 2026. This is the shared series' cadence, not a separate daily release.

reports.title: Remittance inflows statistics and framing
reports.publisher: Derived from Cash Consortium and related sources
reports.description: Statistics and framing of remittance inflows. Remittances have become the principal source of hard currency after the collapse of oil exports, estimated at over USD 7 billion in recent years and exceeding 30% of GDP. They are a critical household survival and external-financing mechanism.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality external-financing node under current conditions. Replaces oil as the dominant hard-currency source.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank indicator page 'Personal remittances, received (current US$)' for Yemen, Rep. Caveat: the official series ends in 2016; the item's >USD 7bn figure comes from the Cash Consortium of Yemen, an NGO consortium that is not an official statistical publisher.
reports._cadence_evidence: World Bank Open Data indicator page (BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT) - a live queryable catalog entry with CSV/XML/Excel download and DataBank access; no discrete edition or stated release cycle (series shown 1990-2016).
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Internal displacement statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix and OCHA sources
reports.description: Statistics on internal displacement. Yemen hosts one of the world’s largest IDP populations; new displacement continues even in periods of relative de-escalation, with Ma’rib and other governorates as major destinations.
reports._url_evidence: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix Yemen country page listing Rapid Displacement Tracking, Area Assessment, Flow Monitoring Registry and MCLA products plus the Annual DTM Displacement Report and National Displacement Profile.
reports._cadence_evidence: IOM DTM Yemen page's flagship product is the Rapid Displacement Tracking (RDT) update, published weekly (alongside monthly Flow Monitoring Registry, quarterly Area Assessments and an annual report); 60+ dated products listed, most recent shown July 2024.

reports.title: Agriculture production statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from national and USDA/FAO-aligned sources
reports.description: Statistics on crop production. Sorghum, millet, wheat and other cereals are produced at low absolute levels relative to national food needs; Yemen is heavily import-dependent for staple cereals. Agriculture remains important for rural livelihoods under severe water and conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node under import dependence and conflict stress.
reports._url_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Yemen (dated June 2026) giving 2025 cereal production of about 400,000 tonnes, wheat and sorghum crop notes, and 2026 cereal import requirements of 5.2 million tonnes.
reports._cadence_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Yemen, current issue reference date 04-June-2026; the linked PDF archive (YEM_Archive.pdf) lists ~16 dated editions across 2015-2025, i.e. roughly one to three per year, averaging about 1.5.

reports.title: Fiscal balance and revenue statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from IMF-aligned and national fiscal monitoring
reports.description: Fiscal revenue, expenditure and balance indicators. Government revenues (excluding grants) have collapsed relative to pre-war levels; deficits are financed under extreme constraint with heavy reliance on grants and limited domestic sources. Dual control further fragments fiscal capacity.
reports._notes: Core fiscal-flow node under extreme revenue collapse and dual institutions.
reports._url_evidence: Central Bank of Yemen annual report series page; the 2024 report contains Chapter Three 'المالية العامة' (Public Finance) alongside the external sector chapter, the only regularly published official fiscal accounts. Covers IRG-controlled fiscal space only.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same CBY page as the BOP item (pages/31): the Annual Reports series, one edition per year (2020, 2022-2025), which is where the fiscal/external tables sit.

reports.title: Education disruption and out-of-school statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from UNICEF and education monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics and framing of education access under conflict. Millions of children remain out of school; thousands of schools are damaged or destroyed. Continuously cited in humanitarian and human-capital analysis.
reports._notes: Core education densification under conflict disruption.
reports._url_evidence: UNICEF Yemen education programme page stating around 2 million children out of school and 2,916 schools destroyed, damaged or used for non-educational purposes.
reports._cadence_evidence: UNICEF Yemen education page is a static programme description - no publication date, no dated editions, no version numbering and no stated update schedule.

reports.title: Health access and nutrition statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from UNICEF / WHO and humanitarian sources
reports.description: Statistics on health-service access and malnutrition. Large shares of the population lack access to basic healthcare; severe acute malnutrition among children remains a critical emergency indicator.
reports._notes: Core health and nutrition densification under humanitarian emergency conditions.
reports._url_evidence: UNICEF Yemen nutrition page giving 2.2 million children with acute malnutrition, 540,000 with severe acute malnutrition, and support to 4,465 primary health care facilities and 34 therapeutic feeding centres.
reports._cadence_evidence: UNICEF Yemen nutrition page is a static programme description with illustrative 2021-2022 figures; states no release frequency, dated editions or update schedule.

reports.title: Major merchandise trade partners statistics
reports.description: Statistics on major trade partners. China, Saudi Arabia, India, Turkey and Brazil are leading import origins (food, fuel, consumer and intermediate goods); India and Saudi Arabia feature among top export destinations for residual non-oil goods. The trade deficit is large and structural.
reports._notes: Core formal trade-partner densification under constrained volumes.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank WITS Yemen trade summary; page lists top export partners (Egypt 49.58%, Turkey 28.02%, Oman 10.53%) and top import partners (UAE 24.04%, China 10.38%, Saudi Arabia 6.46%) with exports USD 24m against imports USD 4,716m.
reports._cadence_evidence: WITS (World Integrated Trade Solution) country profile is a live queryable trade database with user-selected year ranges; the only temporal metadata is a per-indicator 'Last Updated | DEC-12-2024' stamp, not a release cycle.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions.
